assessments.reasoning: The Kotlin/Core inheritance chapter ties subclassing to open or abstract status and makes closure the class default. It separately assigns abstract status to a sealed class even when the declaration omits the abstract keyword.

challenge.method: Test the default against a sealed declaration and check whether every class kind can opt into inheritance.
challenge.results: Implicit abstract status accounts for sealed classes. Data, enum, and annotation classes have a stricter closure rule. The claim gives no unrestricted right to subclass sealed classes.

limitations: The language imposes additional rules for sealed subclasses and for closed class kinds. Interface inheritance is separate.
